title: The supervisor's own SIGTERM stop path settles as failed without the final push
body: internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go handles SIGTERM by stopping the runner and writing runner.exit, but skips the final push the normal exit path makes before settlement — so an attempt signalled directly (not via the container's PID 1, whose flush this tick adds) loses whatever its commits had not pushed since the last timer fire. Not a gap in the eviction story (the platform signals only the main process, and run-epic's flush now pushes), but it is a real asymmetry if a supervisor is ever stopped by hand.
